key_insight: Intrinsic Fréchet means can be approximated on an unknown manifold using only local samples and an observation metric, without explicit knowledge of its intrinsic geometry.
engineering_relevance: The method supports intrinsic averaging of non-Euclidean data, including probability distributions represented in Wasserstein space.
method: Adaptively sample the unknown compact manifold and build graph-based approximations of geodesic interpolation.
Iteratively approximate the intrinsic Fréchet mean with an O(1/T) expected objective gap under stated assumptions.
Extend ISOMAP metric-equivalence guarantees from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments demonstrating effectiveness, but gives no datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
watch_item: The theoretical sample bound, Õ(T^(4d+3)), grows steeply with intrinsic dimension d, raising scalability concerns.
paper_title: Computing Fréchet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
